Notation (E477): ∫1/z^m (1/y^n) = Σ_{z≥1} z^{-m} Σ_{y≤z} y^{-n}, with the diagonal y=z included; ∫1/z^k = ζ(k). With this convention ∫1/z^2(1/y) = ζ(2,1)+ζ(3) = 2ζ(3).

Top of page: the table of §22 (previous page) is put in general form. For order m+n = λ with n = 1:
2 Σ_z H_z / z^{λ-1} = (λ+1) ζ(λ) − Σ_{k=2}^{λ-2} ζ(k) ζ(λ−k).
In modern terms this is Euler's evaluation of the linear Euler sum: 2 S_{1,q} = (q+2) ζ(q+1) − Σ_{j=1}^{q-2} ζ(j+1) ζ(q−j), with q = λ−1. Equivalently, for the strict double zeta value, ζ(λ−1,1) = ((λ−1)/2) ζ(λ) − ½ Σ_{k=2}^{λ-2} ζ(k) ζ(λ−k).

§23: The second method proved the formula only for odd λ, by enumeration of the m+n-odd orders. Euler had 'interpolated' it to even λ. To check that this interpolation is legitimate, he compares the interpolated formulas for even λ with the expressions already obtained for even orders by the first method. Eliminating the double sums leaves relations among the even zeta values alone:
- 5ζ(4) = 2ζ(2)^2
- 7ζ(6) = 4ζ(2)ζ(4)
- 9ζ(8) = 4ζ(2)ζ(6) + 2ζ(4)^2
- in general (2n+1) ζ(2n) = Σ_{k=1}^{n-1} 2 ζ(2k) ζ(2n−2k), each unordered pair appearing twice.

Writing ζ(2k) = α_k π^{2k} (α, β, γ, δ, ε, …), he recovers the recursion he had proved earlier for these coefficients: 5β = 2α², 7γ = 4αβ, …, 15η = 4αζ + 4βε + 4γδ. Agreement with known results is taken as confirmation of the interpolation. The purpose is a consistency check of a heuristic extension from odd to even weight; it also yields a new derivation of the convolution recursion for ζ(2n), i.e. the Bernoulli-number convolution identity.
